title: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

reading.body:
This is an AI-altered image of real people published as though it were a photograph. The alteration happened in the production of advertising banners, where a picture taken at a 2024 Lunar New Year event was reused. One student's likeness was replaced with an image of a Black woman, and two other students were made to look thinner. The banner carried no indication that the image had been altered.

The failure sits in the review and publication of the image, not in the tool. Stanford's policy already banned using AI to produce or alter images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities or achievements, so the rule that would have stopped the banner existed before the banner ran. Catching it required a person to compare the published image against the original photograph and to confirm that any alteration was disclosed. Stanford says it is adding training and improving review of all materials, which is the point at which the check was absent.

It is not established who made the alteration, why it was made, or whether anyone has faced consequences. The university has confirmed the AI use and called it a violation of its policy, and that confirmation is not a finding of intent.

reports.title: Stanford Used A.I. to Swap Black Student for Hispanic Student in a Photo
Stanford R&DE Uses AI to Race Swap Students for Advertising
University confirms use of AI-edited photo amid controversy
Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

summary:
In 2024, a Stanford photographer took a picture of Billy Ramirez, a Hispanic student, with two other students at a Lunar New Year event. The dining service posted it online. When Stanford used the image on banners last week, Ramirez had been replaced by an image of a Black woman, and the other two students were made to look thinner. Ramirez, a senior majoring in human biology, learned about the change from a friend and said he was upset and frustrated.

Stanford said on Tuesday that it had used artificial intelligence to alter the original image. The university said its policy strictly bans using AI to produce or alter images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities, or achievements. It said the alteration and the failure to disclose it violated that policy. Stanford is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises to add training and improve review of all materials.
title_en: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad
